summary: An absent prompt file throws a raw ENOENT out of `Dispatcher.tick()`, so `flume tick` exits 1 and `flume loop` spends 50 children on it where `flume render` calls the same chain mount-dead
acceptance: a phase whose declared prompt file is absent or unreadable ends the tick in the mount-dead class — `flume tick` exits `69` naming the path, and `flume loop` halts there instead of spending its remaining children on an input that resolved once and will resolve the same way again, which is the fate `flume render` already gives that chain. The refusal is the load's own named class; no verb reaches it through a raw stack.
